title: Reporter context pack and research assignment on a Story
description:
Ryan 2026-11-03: move from generating ideas to researching the ideas editors select. An editor attaches a research assignment with their own direction to a Story; a reporting agent works with the Story, its References, its messages and the desk's context. This pack is the first of a series for newsroom agents.

MODULE `src/papyrus_content/newsroom_context_pack.py`. `build_context_pack(store, *, profile, assignment=None, story_lineage_id, direction=None, max_characters=None) -> dict`, contract `newsroom-context-pack/v1`. `PROFILES` holds `reporter` as an ordered layer list plus its role text, so other agents can be added by data. Deterministic and no model calls. Do not use `papyrus_newsroom.newsroom.papyrus_build_assignment_agent_context`, which predates sections.

Output: `system` (text), `user` (text), `layers` (per layer: name, entries with source ids, characters, droppedCount, droppedReason), `warnings`, `contextHash` (sorted compact JSON sha256 of rendered content and provenance, excluding fetch time, same way as editorial_context), `editorialContextHash`.

SYSTEM, never trimmed: role text, then `resolve_editorial_context` (publication mission and policy, section mission, policy, assignment guidance, kill criteria). Missing section mission or policy is a warning in `warnings`, not an invented default. If required policy is unavailable, stop, as editorial context already does.

USER LAYERS, in this order, most specific first:
1. `assignment`: editor's direction, title, who asked.
2. `story`: title, deck, latest version body, stage, type, section.
3. `story_references`: `uses_evidence` and consulted References: title, URL, summary, published date, accept reason, stars, and accepted edge notes (see memory rule: human relationships and their notes are first-class).
4. `story_conversation`: Messages on the Story's threads (anchor `item#<lineage>`, kinds `story_reporting` and `story_conversation`), oldest first, with author.
5. `desk_published`: published Stories in the same section, newest first: title, deck, date, address.
6. `desk_references`: accepted References with this curation section. Rank: human vote or stars first (stars, then a written reason), then newest. Auto-accepted ones rank below human ones. Rejected and pending never appear.
7. `publication_published`: published Stories in other sections.
8. `publication_references`: accepted References in other sections, same rank.

Exclude `SYSTEM_ITEM_TYPES`, retired Items, the Story itself and References already in layer 3 from outer layers. Everything is tenant-scoped via the client.

BUDGET. No fixed counts or day windows (rule: no arbitrary limits). `max_characters` is the only bound, from the model's real context limit. Layers 1-4 are filled first. If layers 1-4 alone exceed it, trim from layer 4's oldest messages then layer 3's summaries, and record it. The remainder is shared top-down in halves: layer 5 may use up to half of what remains, layer 6 half of what is then left, and so on, with unused room rolling forward, so outer layers shrink but are not starved. Whole entries only. Record `droppedCount` per layer. Reads are newest first and stop once a layer's share is full.

CLI, following `assignments_commands.py` conventions; `papyrus` writes unless `--dry-run`:
- `papyrus assignments context-pack --story <lineage> [--assignment <id>] [--direction TEXT] [--format text|json] [--max-characters N]`: read only.
- `papyrus stories assign-research --story <lineage> --direction TEXT|--direction-file F [--type research.multi] [--title T] [--dry-run]`: creates an Assignment with `itemLineageId`, the Story's section, the direction in `instructions` and `metadata`, default title from the Story, default type `research.multi`, `contextProfile: reporter`. An `idea` Story moves to stage `assignment` through the existing recorded stage move; other stages stay. Default status open. Records an AssignmentEvent.

RESEARCH RUN. In `multi_search_research.py`, when the assignment has `itemLineageId`: build the `reporter` pack, prepend `pack.system` to PLAN_SYSTEM and SYNTH_SYSTEM, and use `pack.user` as the brief, so queries and synthesis know the Story, the editor's direction and what the publication already covers. Assignments with no Story behave exactly as now. Packet metadata records `contextHash`, `editorialContextHash` and per-layer sizes. Verify and fix if needed: the packet Message is on the Story's thread so the Work trail shows it; proposed sources become Reference records through the existing intake and are linked to the Story as consulted, not cited; Story text is never changed. Confirm the model is the default GPT-6 Luna.

SPECS. Narrative Gherkin in `features_backend/newsroom-context-pack.feature`, with steps using a fake store, covering: layer order; system never trimmed under a tiny budget; missing section doctrine warns; rejected and pending References never appear; human-rated rank above auto-accepted; the halving share keeps outer layers present and they drop first; dropped counts reported; hash stable across runs and changing when policy changes; tenant isolation; a Story with no section (desk layers empty, warning, publication layers still fill); assign-research creates the link, moves only idea Stories, and dry-run writes nothing; research run uses the pack when a Story is linked and is unchanged when not. Add a section to `docs/story-reporting.md`. No network and no real content in tests.
